controls.reason: The catalog cannot prove it contains every data set across databases, files, exports, replicas, analytics, devices, and shadow stores.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An analyst creates a production customer CSV outside the catalog with no owner or classification. Every catalog row is complete, so the proposal passes while the universal claim is false.

controls.reason: The proposed relationship registry is not authoritative for every logical, application-enforced, cross-store, and dynamically created reference.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An application stores an unenforced customer ID in a document field omitted from the relationship registry. All listed relationships have constraints or jobs, so the checker passes while referential integrity is neither enforced nor checked there.

controls.reason: Queue completeness and all blocking modes are not bounded; one configured poison test cannot prove that a message never blocks a queue indefinitely under other partitions, priorities, or consumer states.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unlisted priority queue retries a malformed head message forever while later messages wait. Every inventoried queue has finite retries and the tested queue passes, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: A declared index inventory can omit indexes, and active monitor bindings do not prove every production index has meaningful freshness and reconciliation coverage.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A search index created manually in another account is absent from the inventory and has no freshness monitor. All listed indexes have green signals, so the checker passes.

controls.reason: The schema inventory cannot enumerate every serialized, unstructured, computed, embedded, and application-level date value, and declared column types do not prove actual stored values are unambiguous.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A JSON text field stores local timestamps without offsets but is not classified as a time field. Every inventoried time column uses the allowlist, so the checker passes while ambiguous times remain.

controls.reason: One registry entry labelled for each dimension does not prove the indicators meaningfully cover the data, populations, failure modes, or decisions implied by data quality.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Five indicators are mapped to the required labels but each returns the constant value 100 without reading data. The registry check passes although no dimension is actually covered.

controls.reason: Existing detector executions do not prove complete relationship scope or that each query can detect real orphans in all relevant partitions and stores.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An orphan query checks only the first tenant and reports zero; orphan rows exist for another tenant. The current execution and explicit count satisfy the clauses while orphaned references remain undetected.

controls.reason: Audit evidence is not an authority for manual changes that bypass or disable that same audit path, so the every-event premise is circular.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A database administrator disables auditing, edits a balance, and reenables it. Every event visible in the audit source has authorization, so the proposal passes while the unaudited manual change violates the rule.

controls.reason: The migration inventory cannot prove it contains ad hoc scripts, console changes, vendor migrations, or changes performed outside the normal pipeline.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An operator runs an unregistered production ALTER statement without a plan. Every inventoried migration has a reviewed plan, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: The word representative has no objective workload, data shape, environment, concurrency, sample, or acceptance protocol in the proposed proof.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A migration test measures ten empty rows on a laptop and records all named metrics. It passes the clause although production contains billions of rows and very different resource use.

controls.reason: Destructive-change classification and recovery-point usability are not completely defined; a destructive change can be downgraded or a nominal backup can be unusable.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A migration that drops customer history is marked non-destructive, so no backup is required. All records labelled destructive have preceding recovery points, and the checker passes.

controls.reason: A signal-producing exercise does not bound the complete migration inventory or prove real operators can observe progress and failures across production paths.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unregistered vendor migration emits no telemetry, while the single instrumented migration produces both test signals. The proposal passes although that production migration is not observable.

controls.reason: A consumer registry cannot establish every dynamic query, report, external integration, cached client, or unknown downstream consumer.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An external report still reads a deprecated column but is omitted from the registry. All registered consumers completed migration, so removal is allowed and the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Matching artifact digests does not prove the migration was genuinely rehearsed with equivalent parameters, data shape, permissions, configuration, and execution path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Rehearsal runs the same binary with --dry-run on empty data, while production uses --force on live data. Digests match, so both clauses pass although the production migration was not rehearsed.

controls.reason: The privacy inventory can omit categories, and a nonempty lawful-basis reference does not establish a valid lawful basis or authorization.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Biometric data is missing from the inventory, while every listed category has populated fields including a bogus authorization reference. The proposal passes despite missing and legally invalid records.

controls.reason: The change registry cannot prove it identifies every new use, and completion of a privacy-review record does not establish that specialist privacy review was valid.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A team reuses location data for advertising without registering the use. Every registered use has a pre-activation review, so the checker passes.

controls.reason: Complete intake across email, portals, support, agents, and jurisdictions is not bounded; requests missing from the record system evade deadline tracking.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A deletion request arrives by support chat and is never registered. All recorded requests have due and status timestamps, so the proposal passes while that request deadline is untracked.

controls.reason: An authoritative inventory cannot be assumed complete for every data category, so categories without a retention entry can disappear from evaluation.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A new analytics category is collected but omitted from the inventory and has no retention period. Every catalogued category has a machine-readable rule, so the checker passes.

controls.reason: The statement is an existence-only requirement, and the proposed bounded record exactly requires named primary and escalation contacts, a reachable route, and an ordered path.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried stale or empty contact records: they fail the current reachable-route and required-field checks. The statement does not require judging the quality of privacy advice or escalation decisions.

controls.reason: The downstream-tool and identity mapping is inherently incomplete unless every transfer and shadow tool is enumerated by an independent authority.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A deleted user remains in an unregistered support SaaS account. All mapped tools satisfy the retention limit, so the proposal passes while the user remains downstream indefinitely.

controls.reason: The proposal does not define objective applicability for frontend-only, backend-only, installed, batch, or multi-tier systems, so a valid result cannot be computed uniformly.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A backend-only service has no frontend layer. The checker either invents a fake frontend budget or fails despite the control being inapplicable; the primary proposal has no bounded Not Applicable decision.

controls.reason: Quantifying over launch records does not prove every real launch is registered, so an unrecorded launch can lack a baseline without affecting the check.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A feature is enabled publicly without a launch record or baseline. Every existing launch record points to a pre-launch measurement, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: The public-page inventory can omit dynamic, localized, authenticated, campaign, and alternate-domain pages, making target compliance partial.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A slow public campaign page is absent from the inventory while all listed pages meet their approved targets. Both clauses pass although not every public page meets targets.

controls.reason: The endpoint and journey inventory cannot prove complete coverage of dynamic routes, versions, internal gateways, and composite journeys.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A newly exposed endpoint is omitted and has no latency target. Every catalogued endpoint has a percentile and threshold, so the checker passes.

controls.reason: A database inventory can omit unmanaged and embedded stores, and current samples do not show that all relevant query activity is measured.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A production SQLite store is absent from monitoring. Every listed database has current latency and volume samples, so the proposal passes while its queries are unmeasured.

controls.reason: The interface inventory cannot prove it contains every payload path, and one boundary test does not establish limits for alternate encodings, streams, compression, and chained messages.
controls.counterexample_analysis: An unregistered file-upload route accepts unlimited chunked data. All inventoried JSON endpoints reject oversized bodies, so the proposal passes while payloads are unbounded.

controls.reason: The approved policy fully defines cold state, workload, metric, percentile, and numeric threshold, and authenticated evidence executes that exact bounded protocol.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried changing the region, warm state, percentile, or workload to hide a slow start; each change breaks equality with the approved protocol. Broader user satisfaction is outside this threshold-specific control.

controls.reason: Third-party discovery is not complete across tags, SDKs, network calls, providers, and runtime injection, so unlisted services evade measurement.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A marketing tag injects a fourth-party script omitted from the inventory. Every listed third party has an impact result, so the proposal passes while that script is unmeasured.

controls.reason: The control requires automated release thresholds, and the authoritative pipeline exposes exact numeric thresholds while a failing fixture proves the gate enforces them.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a threshold that only warns or a test disconnected from the release pipeline; those fail the authoritative-gate and deliberately failing-fixture checks. The statement does not prescribe which metrics or values humans must approve.

controls.reason: The statement is a documentation requirement over six explicitly named traffic conditions, and the record requires numeric value, unit, horizon, source, and owner for each.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried unrealistic forecast values: quality may be poor, but the narrow control asks that the conditions be forecast, not that the forecast be accurate. Missing any named scenario or field fails.

controls.reason: The rule asks for recorded growth forecasts for the named dimensions, and the clause requires numeric values, units, horizons, assumptions, and owners for all of them.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A wrong growth estimate does not defeat this documentation-only classification because accuracy is not promised. Omitting queue or backup growth fails the exact closed-field check.

controls.reason: The proposal leaves scenario applicability and real authentication or authorization overhead undefined; an enabled flag or approved mock does not prove production overhead is included.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A load test uses a stub identity service that returns instantly but labels the authentication path enabled. The transcript passes while real token validation and policy lookup overhead are absent.

controls.reason: An approved scenario contract can omit a real external dependency, and a referenced behavior profile need not reproduce production latency, errors, quotas, or correlated failure.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The contract excludes a fraud provider and simulates all listed dependencies as zero-latency successes. The transcript passes while actual external dependency behavior is absent.

controls.reason: One stress path beyond one approved boundary cannot identify how the system fails across data shapes, bottlenecks, failure domains, durations, and overload modes.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A short CPU-heavy test records CPU saturation, but a long connection-heavy load causes corrupt timeouts first. The bounded evidence passes while another real beyond-capacity failure remains unidentified.

controls.reason: An approved forecast supplies the exact largest expected tenant profile and the authenticated fixture must meet or exceed every declared size dimension.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried testing a smaller or differently shaped tenant; it fails the dimension comparison. Whether the forecast itself is wise is an accountable planning question outside this inclusion-only test.

controls.reason: The provider-resource inventory can omit resources, subaccounts, regions, and soft or undocumented limits, so the review join is not exhaustive.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A production messaging quota in a separate project is absent from the inventory and unreviewed. All listed provider resources have dated reviews, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: The clauses do not establish a complete database and resource inventory, so a saturated pool, replica, storage tier, or I/O path can be omitted from the required set.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A read-replica connection pool is missing from capacity evidence and has no headroom. All declared database resources meet policy thresholds, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: The required platform-resource set is not independently complete, allowing queues, caches, networks, workers, and load balancers to be omitted before threshold comparison.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A manually created worker pool is at 100% capacity but absent from the capacity record. Every declared resource meets its threshold, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: Repository configuration is not a complete autoscaler inventory and bounded tests may omit provider-created, manual, external, or alternate failure-path scalers.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A cloud autoscaler created in the console is absent from IaC and oscillates during scale-down. Every repository autoscaler has passing tests, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: The scaling contract is allowed to define which dependencies can be pressured, so an omitted dependency and behavior outside the approved envelope evade proof of the absolute statement.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A search service is missing from the dependency list and is overloaded during scale-out. All declared limits stay green in the approved test envelope, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: The original explicitly scopes sufficiency according to the approved design, which defines applicable failure scenarios and numeric requirements, and the evidence must satisfy every declared scenario.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried omitting a region scenario from a design that declares regional survival; that fails the every-scenario check. A system intentionally designed only for node loss is judged against that bounded design, as the statement requires.

controls.reason: The queue inventory can omit queues and alternate creation paths, so numeric bounds and overload tests cover only discovered objects.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A dynamically created tenant queue is missing from inventory and grows without limit. Every listed queue has a passing boundary test, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: The edge inventory cannot prove every exposed surface, hostname, origin, protocol, and provider path is included, so review records can be complete only for a partial universe.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A forgotten origin IP is publicly reachable but absent from the edge inventory and has no DDoS review. Every catalogued service has a dated review, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: The statement requires that expected and peak cost be modeled, and the clause exactly requires both scenarios, inputs, horizon, currency, result, ownership, and revision metadata.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried an inaccurate price assumption: it affects model quality, which this statement does not claim. Missing a peak scenario, inputs, computed result, or current owner fails the bounded record check.

controls.reason: Which operations are essential is an accountable business and safety decision, and the approved list may omit a truly essential operation while all listed tests pass.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A billing reconciliation job is wrongly classified nonessential and is silently killed by a cost cap. Every operation labelled essential emits a signal in tests, so the proposal passes.

controls.reason: The capacity registry cannot prove it contains every explicit and implicit assumption embedded in forecasts, code, supplier limits, and operational decisions.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A forecast assumes a provider will double a quota but the assumption is absent from the registry and has no owner or review date. Every registered assumption has both fields, so the proposal passes.
